steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease cookie sheets.

In a large bowl, cream together the butter, brown sugar and white sugar until light and fluffy. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well with each addition. Combine the cocoa, flour, and baking soda, gradually stir into the creamed mixture. Finally, fold in white chocolate chips. Drop by rounded spoonfuls onto the prepared cookie sheets.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes in the preheated oven, until puffy but still soft. Allow cookies to cool on baking sheet for 5 minutes before removing to a wire rack to cool completely.

review.reviewBody: In my circle of friends it's a well known fact that I can bake anything except cookies. So you can imagine everyones surprise when they tasted these fabulous, chocolatey, yummy cookies. Finally, a cookie I can make without them being little crispy rocks. Update: I made these again today but copied the recipe down wrong and used baking powder instead of baking soda. Found the answer to the problem of them going flat. They came out all puffy and pretty. Next time I'll try half baking soda/half baking powder to see if it might improve the texture while maintaining shape.

I followed the recipe as is except to try the recommended 1 t baking soda plus 1 t baking powder...I did not want them to flatten. They came out great...about 8 min in a convection oven at 325. firm edges with softer center and puffy, very chocolatey!

Followed the suggestions made by several others - changed 2 tsp baking soda to 1 tsp baking soda, 1 baking powder and added 1 tsp vanilla. I realized way after it was all down that I should have added a tsp of salt. I also added about 1/4 cup of walnuts for crunch. My husband ate 4 while they were barely cool. Delicious!! 
I think my oven is slow, or maybe it is because I live in a humid climate, but I did bake them for the full 10 minutes. Cookies were soft and chewy. I would love to figure out how to make these crispy.

Delicious cookies. I haven't actually made them with white chocolate chips yet. I did one batch with salted caramel chips and toffee bits, and another batch with Reese's Pieces. Both were delicious. This recipe has more cocoa powder than others, and this makes the cookies very fudgy and good. I did use 1 tsp of baking powder and 1 tsp of baking soda instead of 2 tsp of baking soda, and they are wonderful. I make my batter a day before I need them, and I spoon it onto a cookie sheet with wax paper and freeze them before I cook them. I cook them straight out of the freezer at 350 for 11 minutes. They are very soft when the come out, but after they cool, they are very gooey and chewy, and crisp on the outside. Very good cookies. This will be my new chocolate cookie recipe. Thanks.

Fudgy delicious, like a brownie cookie! I added 2t vanilla and 1/4t salt, plus 12 oz salted caramel chips. I used an overflowing 2 oz ice cream scoop for the batter but the cookies did not spread as they baked, so I used a butter knife to flatten subsequent batches.

The first time I made these exactly as written, and found them to be ok but not great. They were too dry and too cakey. The second time I made them I used baking powder instead of baking soda, and under-measured the flour. I also added a tsp of vanilla. The batter still looked too dry to me so I threw in some water a teaspoon at a time until it was a better consistency. I used 1/2 cup white chocolate chips and 1/2 semi-sweet. I was worried that they wouldn't turn out after all the tinkering with the batter, but they were amazing. Fudgy and moist, with a flatter shape and more cookie-like texture. Will definitely make them again with my changes.

Not sure about some of the negative comments, I experiment with new cookie recipes all the time and this one’s a winner. I did add a teaspoon of vanilla and instead of the white chocolate chips I used mini semi-sweet chocolate chips and Andes crème de menthe baking chips. Oh my, what a decadent cookie for the Christmas cookie tray.

I did tweak to modify: 

Add:
1 tsp Vanilla
1 tsp Salt
1 package chocolate pudding
1 tsp Baking Soda

Reduce Flour to 1 1/4 cup

Baked for 9 minutes. It wasn't too sweet. I initially thought that would be a problem. It was slightly crips on the edges and moist in the middle. 

Delicious and would make again. My co-workers loved it.

I made no substitutions at all, but I did follow one reviewers note to not over bake. I left my cookies in for 9 minutes, took them out, let them sit for two minutes on the cookie sheet and then put them on the cooling rack. These were as delicious as promised, chocolatey and scrumptious! I will definitely make these again and again, great recipe!

I made these because I was looking for a chocolate cookie recipe where I can use the rest of my leftover m&m's (I've had sitting around for a year).

They turned out better than I expected. I only used a 1/2 cup of brown sugar instead of 3/4 cup, about a 1/2 tsp. of salt, a Tbs. of strong brewed coffee, a little over half a cup m&m's, a half cup white chips, a cup of semi sweet chips and a cup of chopped walnuts. They are fantastic!

My husband rarely, if ever, goes to the cookie jar to help himself to cookies. I think he's eaten half the jar by himself.

Tasty cookies! I also substituted 1 tsp. baking powder and 1 tsp. baking soda for the original 2 tsp. baking soda. And, (because I had them), I used 1 cup of milk chocolate chips and 1 cup of white chocolate chips instead of 2 cups white chocolate chips. The cookies were soft, moist and delicious! I was expecting them to be hard or crunchy, but the key is to not overbake them. Will definitely use this recipe again!
Made these for my grands. They were a huge hit. Came out perfectly and tasted amazing.
I used half baking powder and half baking soda, added 1 tsp vanilla. Baked 8-9 minutes. Next time I will try peanut butter chips.
This is my favorite cookie recipe

I made them and it came so good. I have made cookies before but they were unsuccessful.but these came perfectly and so tasty.I use some advices from comments like using 1 spoon of baking powder and baking soda.

These were my first cookies I've baked and turned out well! I didn't have baking powder/soda so only used the flour and had to adjust it,but overall am in love![Also had to decrease the white chocolate chips bc I didn't have alot but still!] Would bake them again!!
It was also great as double chocolate with chocolate chips. Also good with peanut butter chips.
Added vanilla and 6 oz of dried cranberries, tastes like a cherry cordial. So delicious
So yummy. Easy to make. Will definitely make again.
